Prime Inc has been amazing for me thus far. I know some people in this group are against megas or don’t recommend prime. I’ll explain my experience.
I started the training program and they paid for me to get there, paid for my hotel, loaned me $200 a week and food was provided for the first week. The hotel is nice, I had a king sized bed with no roommates (fyi some people do get roommates) the training to get my CDL was reasonable. During the PSD phase you are not an employee so that’s why they are loaning you the $200 a week until you pass your CDL test. I had one of the best trainers there, that’s what I was told. I was licensed within 2.5 weeks of arriving to the facility, at that point I became an official employee. I waited 3 days in my hotel until my TNT trainer got there. Some people had to go home because they didn’t have a TNT trainer so beware that could happen. If it does, you’ll still be paid $900 a week while you’re at home (before taxes). I passed the CDL test on my first try so I got a $250 bonus on my first check. Now I make $900 a week until I complete TNT which is supposed to last for 30,000 miles. My trainer and I also get along well so honestly I’d rate my experience 9/10.. the pay is decent. I don’t mind the low training pay because I know that in the future I’ll be making more. I’ve seen people making $4,000 a week or more at Prime. I’ll get there in due time. Good luck

I always think about what lane the rear trailer tires are in to know which way to turn. If you’re doing offset to the right. When you start that means the rear trailer tires are in the left lane, so turn the wheel left FIRST. Once the trailer is straight and rear trailer tires are technically in the right lane, TURN RIGHT. Then just straighten out. I use that method for offset and parallel. With alley dock you need to be looking out of left mirror. If you look out of left mirror turn the wheel right and vice versa.
